openings.claim: Shared-tray organization may manufacture demand for finished-envelope checking: cross-reaching interrupts pattern-specific counts, causing shared-material omissions that then require correction. This evaluates a bounded probe; the complete 60-kit intervention remains unproven.
openings.delta: Remove shared access during picking by placing each volunteer's current materials locally on the existing table, while retaining exact assigned quantities, dimensions, envelopes and pattern assignments. The changed causal arrow is organization producing errors and hence checking demand, rather than errors simply requiring more checking.
openings.prediction: With pattern mix matched, local picking should reduce cross-reaching and shared-material omissions together, reducing correction work enough to offset setup. O4 motivates this prediction but does not establish it or the full-session outcome.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is that omissions occur during envelope filling independently of shared picking. Local placement would then reduce cross-reaching without reducing matched-pattern omissions or correction work.
openings.defeat: Matched blocks show substantially fewer cross-reaches with local placement but unchanged or increased shared-material omissions; alternatively, setup plus assembly and checking cannot meet the original 90-minute budget.
openings.probe: The same two volunteers assemble two small matched blocks of actual assigned kits, one with shared access and one with local placement, reversing condition order across volunteers. Volunteers tally cross-reaches, verify contents immediately, and record setup, assembly and correction time. Pencil pattern identifiers on existing envelopes preserve distribution matching. Keep every operation within the existing table and the whole session's 90-minute budget; local placement proceeds only if it fits. Assess all 60 kits and the distribution correction count before claiming success.
assumptions: Matched assigned-pattern blocks are available; the supplied small-batch mixture is unknown.
Local material placement fits the existing table without new equipment; this is unverified.
Setup and volunteer tallying leave enough time for all 60 kits, checking and correction within 90 minutes; this is unverified.
Order reversal sufficiently limits learning effects for this exploratory probe.
